blog.title: Your monthly grocery list, sorted in 10 minutes
sections: Start with the staples

Rice, atta, dal, oil, sugar, tea and spices are the backbone of every kitchen. Write these down first with the pack size you actually finish in a month. Family packs of 5 kg and 10 kg are usually the best value per kilo.
Then the daily-use items
Soap, toothpaste, shampoo, detergent and dishwash run out quietly. Buying them with the monthly groceries means one trip instead of three, and value packs stay cheaper than single bars.
Keep a festival line

Diwali, Navratri, Janmashtami and wedding season each need their own list: pooja items, sweets ingredients, gifting and extra cleaning supplies. Add a line for the month's festival so nothing is left for the last day.
Check what is already at home
Open the kitchen cupboards before you leave. Half-used containers of dal and spices are the most common double purchase we see at the counter.
Shop it in one trip
Both our Virpur and Lalsar branches keep groceries, personal care, home needs, kitchenware and stationery under one roof. Bring the list, tick it off aisle by aisle and go home with everything.

blog.title: MRP vs our price: how to read a shelf label
sections: Two prices, one label
Every shelf label shows the printed MRP and the price you actually pay with us. The difference is your saving on that pack, before any festival offer.
Look at the pack size
A bigger pack with a higher price can still be cheaper per kilo or per litre. Divide the price by the quantity and compare, especially on oil, rice, detergent and atta.
Family packs win most of the time
Value packs of biscuits, soap and noodles are priced for the month, not the day. If your family finishes them, they are the better buy.
Offers are per branch
Stock and offers can differ between Virpur and Lalsar. Our staff will tell you what is running in the branch you are standing in.
Ask at the counter
Not sure which pack is the better deal? Ask. Helping you compare is part of the job and nobody minds the question.

blog.title: Compare brands and unit prices before you buy
sections: Why we stock more than one brand
On most shelves you will find two or three brands of the same product. That is deliberate: it lets you choose between the lowest price, the brand you trust and the pack size your family needs.
Unit price is the fair comparison
Price per kilo, per litre or per piece is the only honest way to compare two packs. A smaller pack can look cheaper while costing more per use.
Where brands matter
For tea, oil and personal care, taste and habit matter and most families stick to a brand. For sugar, salt, garbage bags and plastics, the unit price usually decides.
Where to save without noticing
Store-trusted brands of dal, rice and cleaning products often match the big names at a lower price. Try one pack and see if the family notices.
Bring the question to us
Our staff compare these packs every day. If you want the best value for a wedding, a function or just the month, ask at the counter and we will point you to it.

blog.title: Diwali shopping checklist: pooja, sweets, gifts and cleaning
sections: Cleaning comes first
Diwali starts with the house. Floor cleaner, detergent, scrubbers, garbage bags and fresh buckets go on the list two weeks early so the cleaning does not clash with the cooking.
Pooja needs
Diyas, cotton wicks, ghee, camphor, agarbatti, kumkum and rice for the pooja thali. Our pooja aisle is restocked daily in the festival weeks.
Sweets and farsan ingredients
Besan, ghee, sugar, dry fruits, maida and rava for home-made ladoo, chakri and mathiya. Buy in family packs; the quantities always run higher than planned.
Gifting under one roof
Gift packs of dry fruits, biscuits, tea and kitchenware make easy gifts for neighbours and staff. We keep them near the billing counter in the festival season.
New for the home
Dinner sets, storage containers, pressure cookers and steel bottles are the Diwali purchases families plan all year. Visit early for the best choice of colours and sizes.

blog.title: Navratri ready: seven things every family stocks up on
sections: Fasting staples
Sabudana, singoda flour, rajgira, peanuts and rock salt disappear from shelves in the first two days. Buy them before the first garba night.
Fruits and dry fruits
Bananas, apples, dates and a mix of dry fruits keep energy up through nine nights of garba.
Dairy and ghee
Milk, curd and ghee are used far more during fasting weeks. Keep an extra pack of each in the fridge.
Pooja and decoration
Garba lamps, agarbatti, flowers, kumkum and a fresh chunri for the mandir at home.
Personal care for nine nights
Talcum powder, hair oil, face cream and a good bath soap for the late nights and early mornings.
Snacks for the crowd
Namkeen, chips, biscuits and cold drinks for the family and friends who gather after garba.
Shop it early
Both branches run festival stock from the first week of the month. Early shopping means full shelves and no queues.

blog.title: Back to school: supplies, lunch boxes and bags in one trip
sections: Start with the stationery list
Notebooks, long books, pens, pencils, geometry box, colours and a sharpener. Bring the school's list and tick it off in our stationery aisle.
Lunch boxes and bottles
A steel tiffin and a leak-proof bottle last the whole year. Pick a size the child can carry and clean easily.
School bags
Padded straps, two compartments and a bottle pocket. We stock sizes for nursery through college.
Personal care for the term
Small packs of talcum, hair oil and soap for hostel bags, plus a pack of handwash for the home.
One trip, done
School shopping in a district city takes a day. At Hare Krishna Mall it takes an hour, and the kids can choose their own bag.

blog.title: Monsoon essentials: keep the home dry, clean and stocked
sections: Storage that keeps damp out
Airtight containers for dal, rice, flour and spices stop the monsoon damp from spoiling a month of groceries.
Cleaning and disinfecting
Floor cleaner, toilet cleaner and phenyl go further in the rains. Keep an extra bottle of each and a spare mop.
Mosquito protection
Repellent machines, refills, coils and nets are stocked in both branches from the first rains.
Dry snacks and tea
Namkeen, biscuits and tea powder in sealed packs for the days when nobody wants to step out.
Plastics for the season
Buckets, mugs, tubs and footwear stands for muddy feet at the door.

blog.title: Buy in bulk, plan ahead: family packs that save money
sections: Which items to buy big
Rice, atta, sugar, oil, detergent and tea are used daily and keep well. These are the packs where buying 5 kg or 10 kg at once saves the most.
Which items to buy small
Spices, snacks and dairy lose freshness. Buy the pack you will finish in two or three weeks.
After harvest, before festivals
Many families in our towns stock up after the harvest and before Diwali. Planning the big purchase for those weeks keeps the monthly budget steady.
Storage first
Big packs need airtight containers and a dry shelf. Our kitchen aisle has container sets sized for 5 kg and 10 kg packs.
Ask about multi-pack prices
For functions and weddings we can help with crates of cold drinks, cartons of biscuits and bulk packs of oil and rice. Ask at the counter in Virpur or Lalsar.

blog.title: Wedding season shopping: kitchenware, gifting and the big list
sections: The kitchen list
Pressure cookers, large tawas, big steel vessels, serving spoons and dinner sets for feeding a house full of relatives.
Gifting for guests
Dry-fruit packs, tea gift packs, steel bottles and container sets make practical gifts. We keep them together in the festive weeks.
Groceries in bulk
Rice, oil, ghee, sugar, besan and dry fruits in bulk packs for the sweets and the feast. Ask about multi-pack prices at the counter.
Cleaning before the guests
Floor cleaner, detergent, fresh buckets, mops and garbage bags so the house is ready before the first guest arrives.
Personal care for the family
Soap, shampoo, face cream, talcum and hair oil in family packs for the week of ceremonies.
One trip to one store
Everything above is under one roof at our Virpur and Lalsar branches, so the wedding list does not need a day trip to the city.

faqTabs.name: General Information
qa: What is Hare Krishna Mall?

Hare Krishna Mall (Hare Krishna Supermarket on our logo) is a family-run supermarket with two established branches, Virpur and Lalsar, in Gujarat. We bring the big-city supermarket experience to our towns and the villages around them.
Do you have a physical store?
Yes, two: the main branch in Virpur and the Lalsar branch nearby. Both are open and fully stocked; find them on Google Maps from the Contact page.
What areas do you serve?
Virpur, Lalsar and the villages around both towns. Families from nearby villages do their weekly and monthly shopping with us.
How can I contact Hare Krishna Mall?
Message us on Instagram @hare_krishna_mall_ or visit either branch. Directions for both stores are on the Contact page.
Are you opening more branches?
More branches are planned, but the locations are not decided yet. Follow our Instagram for announcements.

faqTabs.name: Stores & Shopping
qa: Which branch should I visit?
Whichever is closer. Virpur is the main branch; Lalsar serves the villages around it. Both carry groceries, snacks, personal care, home needs, kitchenware, pooja items and stationery.
Do you deliver to homes?
Right now we are an in-store supermarket. For bulk or function orders, speak to the staff at the branch and we will see what is possible.
Is parking available?
Both branches are on the main road of their town with space for two-wheelers and cars nearby. Use the Google Maps links for directions.
Can I order in bulk for a wedding or function?
Yes. Crates of cold drinks, cartons of biscuits and bulk packs of rice, oil and sugar can be arranged. Ask at the counter in advance.
Do you stock seasonal items?
Yes. Navratri, Diwali, Uttarayan, Holi, monsoon and wedding-season stock arrives in the weeks before each season.

faqTabs.name: Payments & Offers
qa: Which payment methods are accepted?
Please check at the billing counter of your branch for the payment modes currently accepted.
How do your prices compare to the city?
Our model is city-style variety at fair prices, close to home. Shelf labels show the printed MRP next to our price so you can see the saving.
Are offers the same in both branches?
Stock and offers can differ between Virpur and Lalsar. Our staff will tell you what is running in the branch you are in.
Do you have family packs?
Yes. Rice, atta, oil, sugar, detergent, biscuits and soap all come in family and value packs that are cheaper per kilo.
How do I hear about new offers?
Follow @hare_krishna_mall_ on Instagram, where we post festival offers and new arrivals.

faqTabs.name: Products & Quality
qa: What do you sell?
Groceries and staples, snacks and beverages, personal care, home and cleaning products, kitchenware and plastics, pooja items and stationery. Seasonal and festive goods come in through the year.
Do you stock well-known brands?
Yes, alongside value brands, so you can choose between the brand you trust and the best unit price.
How fresh is the stock?
Shelves are restocked daily and every pack carries its printed date. Tell our staff if you ever find otherwise.
Can I ask for something you do not stock?
Yes. Tell the staff at the counter and we will try to bring it in for both branches.
Do you sell loose items?
Most groceries are sold in sealed packs so the weight and date are clear. Ask at the branch for anything sold by weight.

faqTabs.name: Returns & Refunds
qa: Can I exchange a product?
Bring your bill to the branch where you bought it and our staff will help with an exchange as per store policy.
What if an item is damaged or wrong?
Damaged or wrong items are exchanged first. Please bring the item and the bill to the same branch.
Are opened packs returnable?
Packaged goods must be unopened and in their original packing for an exchange.
Do I need the bill?
Yes, the bill is needed for any exchange or refund.
How long do I have?
Please come back as soon as you notice a problem; the staff will guide you on what applies to that item.

faqTabs.name: Instagram & Support
qa: Where can I follow you?
On Instagram at @hare_krishna_mall_, where we post reels of new stock, offers and festival shopping.
Can I message you with a question?
Yes, send a DM on Instagram or ask any staff member in store.
Do I need an account on this website?
No. This website shows what we stock and where to find us; shopping happens in store.
Who runs Hare Krishna Mall?
It is a family business run from Virpur, with the same family looking after both branches.
How can I give feedback?
Tell us in store or send a message on Instagram. Feedback from our customers decides what we stock next.
